If you are looking for web design Reno NV customers will actually use, start with who those customers are now. Some have lived in the Truckee Meadows all their lives. Many arrived in the last few years for jobs east of town. Both groups pick a plumber, a dentist or a lunch spot the same way: on a phone, in a few seconds.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, who writes and builds every page himself. You see a free demo of your site first, and you pay $497, $997 or $1,997 once.

The industrial park that changed who lives here

East of Reno, in Storey County, the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center covers more than 100,000 acres. The park already had many tenants when Tesla chose it for its Gigafactory, announced in 2014, which became its best-known tenant. Switch began building a data center campus there in 2015, and in 2017 a Google subsidiary bought 1,210 acres in the park.

The region's job recruiter, the Economic Development Authority of Western Nevada (EDAWN), is a private nonprofit founded in 1983 that focuses on companies that export most of what they make. Those employers bring workers, and the workers need everything else: haircuts, car repair, house cleaning, child care, dinner. The Census Bureau counted 264,165 people in Reno in 2020 and estimated 274,915 by July 2023, a rise of about 4%, and a HUD market profile put the Reno metro area at about 505,600 people at the start of 2024.

A family that just moved from another state does not know which shops are good. They search, they read your site, and they decide. That is where a clear website pays for itself.

Midtown and the Riverwalk, the local side of Reno

Away from the casinos, Midtown runs along South Virginia Street south of downtown, with murals, cafes, thrift stores, patio pubs and locally owned shops. Downtown along the Truckee River, the Riverwalk Merchants Association brings together dozens of nearby restaurants, shops, salons and museums, and it hosts a wine walk on the third Saturday of every month.

For these shops a website does three jobs. It confirms you are still open, it tells a visitor which block you are on, and it lists the events that bring people downtown. A wine walk stop that posts its hours and a photo of the storefront is easy to find the next week.

For a Midtown restaurant

Put the menu on the page as text, not a PDF, with today's hours and a tap-to-call button. Add a short note on patio season and private events. That is what a hungry visitor looks for first.

For a photographer or studio

A gallery of real work, the kinds of sessions you shoot, a starting price if you are comfortable sharing one, and a booking form. Lake Tahoe trips bring couples and families who want photos, so say whether you travel there.

Web design for Reno businesses that serve the whole valley

Residents name their part of town when they search. Sparks is its own city, and neighborhoods such as the South Meadows, Northwest Reno, Somersett and Damonte Ranch each have their own feel. Google says local results weigh relevance, distance and prominence. A landscaper or HVAC company whose site names the areas it covers gives Google something to match; one that just says "Northern Nevada" does not.

What each plan covers

Starter, $497 once: five hand-written pages, a lead form that emails you, Google Maps and hours, live in 7 to 14 days. Pro, $997 once: ten pages with a gallery, local SEO with Google Business Profile setup, your Google reviews on the site and 10 researched city pages, so Sparks and the South Meadows can each get their own page. Agency, $1,997 once: keyword research, a page for each town and service worth having delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks, custom design, and setup of an AI phone agent that is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time. Hosting, maintenance and updates cost $49 a month unless you keep an AI agent. You own the site, and we do not sell page counts.

Northern Nevada resources worth a call

  • Nevada SBDCIts main state office is on the University of Nevada, Reno campus in the Ansari Business Building, and its one-on-one advising is free and confidential, in person or by Zoom.
  • Reno + Sparks Chamber of CommerceThe region's chamber has advocated for local businesses since 1919.
  • EDAWNHelpful if you are relocating or expanding a company that sells outside the region.

Common questions

Do you do WordPress web design in Reno?

We do not promise any particular platform. Every site is hand-built, every page is written for your business, and you own the finished site. If you need WordPress, for example because your staff already knows it or a plugin you rely on needs it, say so when you ask for the demo and Maurice will tell you plainly whether it fits.

How much does web design in Reno, NV cost?

Our prices are fixed and paid once: Starter $497, Pro $997, Agency $1,997. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent. Pro's AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month if you keep it.

I just moved my business to Reno. What should the website say first?

What you do, the parts of the valley you cover, and how to reach you, all on the first screen of a phone. Newcomers and longtime residents both search by neighborhood, so name the areas you really serve, such as Sparks, the South Meadows or Northwest Reno. Then make sure your Google Business Profile says the same thing.

Do you have an office in Reno?

No. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy, East Texas, and works with Reno owners by phone, email and shared links. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
